summary: @servicetitan/quick-actions ships preinstall dropper that downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated 700KB payload
details: The package declares `scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs"`. `setup.mjs` is obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style transforms (hex-mangled identifiers such as `_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`, and per-function string-dictionary indirection). At install time it downloads the Bun runtime (v1.3.13) from the oven-sh/bun GitHub releases, unpacks the platform-specific binary to a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a bundled sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB Bun-compiled bundle with hex-obfuscated variable names and a rotated string/number array with a rotation function (`WV8StW`) — classic string-array obfuscation whose behavior cannot be reviewed in place. The package presents itself as a React UI component library, which has no legitimate need to fetch a second language runtime at install and use it to execute an obfuscated bundle. Using a freshly-downloaded alternate runtime to execute an obfuscated payload is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern, designed to bypass Node-based install-time scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
